cards.text: Come on in, friend! This one's a song from the sons of Korah, a family of Levites who praised the LORD, and it opens with God founding a whole CITY. God gave me a planet the size of one bakery and I STILL can't keep the flour off the floor.

cards.question: The sons of Korah open their song with God's city. Where has He founded it?

cards.text: Turns out this city has a name: Zion. And the LORD doesn't just like her gates, friend. He LOVES them.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD loves the gates of Zion less than all the dwellings of Jacob.

cards.text: Then the song stops talking ABOUT the city and starts talking TO her, like she's right there in the room. Hey, I talk to my oven every morning, so no judgment here.

cards.question: The song speaks straight to the city the LORD loves. Fill it in: ___ things are ascribed to you, O city of God.

cards.text: Then the voice changes. God speaks, and He starts naming names: Rahab and Babylon, along with Philistia, Tyre and Cush.

cards.question: True or false: God mentions Rahab and Babylon, Philistia, Tyre and Cush among those who know Him.

cards.text: Wait. WAIT. Babylon? PHILISTIA? Friend, none of these are Israel, and I promise you, God is not done talking about them.

cards.question: God mentions these nations from outside Israel among those who know Him. What does He say when He mentions them?

answers.text: This one was born in Zion
This one is a stranger here

cards.question: It will be said of Zion that this one and that one were born in her. Who will establish Zion?

cards.text: Then the LORD makes it official and writes it down in the register of the peoples. And friend, a list the LORD writes does NOT end up lost in the back of a junk drawer, trust me, I checked every corner of that thing.

cards.question: In the register of the peoples, the LORD will record: This one was born in ___.

cards.text: One more line, friend. And this song doesn't fade out quiet, it goes out with MUSIC.

cards.question: Psalm 87 ends with music. Who's making it?

cards.text: And they proclaim, “All my springs of joy are in You.” Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer getting my joy from rubber band stretching contests, so I can tell you these folks found the REAL spring.

findings.problem: The card says the sons of Korah are a family of Levites who praised the LORD. That fact comes from outside Psalm 87, but the card gives no reference for it. The card cites only Psalm 87:1.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card asks about the line 'This one was born in Zion' (Psalm 87:6). That line already appeared in Psalm 87:4 and was asked about on card 10. The answer, Zion, has also been told on cards 10 and 11, so this card only repeats an earlier question and doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: Card 7 names 'Rahab' in a list of nations but never says who or what Rahab is. In Psalm 87:4, Rahab is a poetic name for Egypt (compare Ps 89:10 and Isa 30:7). Many bakers will think of Rahab of Jericho (Joshua 2), especially since card 9 builds on these being nations that aren't Israel.
findings.question: Should Papa Dorin say on the card that Rahab here stands for Egypt, with a reference like Isa 30:7? Or should that be left to the dictionary pop-up? The 'New people' rule covers people, not poetic names for nations, and identifying Rahab as Egypt is an interpretation the passage itself doesn't state.
